status: post-opening finite trait-response alignment test frozen before endpoint readback
question: Does conventional amphibian life-history functional distance predict how differently species respond to rainfall?

species_response.universe: the 29 direction-blind response-eligible species fixed by the species-pulse analysis
species_response.response: pair-covariate-adjusted wet-versus-dry log-odds intercept fitted from all matched pairs
species_response.eligibility: the original >=40 discordant events across >=10 routes; no species added by response direction

axes: mean log clutch size from litter-size minimum and maximum
mean log offspring size from offspring-size minimum and maximum
functional_space.scaling: z-score across the 42 complete species in the frozen active-community functional panel

primary_test.metric: Mantel-style Pearson correlation between pairwise functional distance and absolute pairwise adjusted rainfall-response difference
primary_test.permutation: 100000 unrestricted permutations of response labels across species; deterministic seed 2842026
primary_test.interpretation_null: rainfall response diversity is largely hidden from this conventional functional trait space

taxonomy_sensitivity.permutation: 100000 response-label permutations within AmphiBIO family; deterministic seed 2842027
taxonomy_sensitivity.purpose: test alignment beyond broad family structure

secondary_descriptives: fraction of opposite-sign species pairs in lowest versus highest functional-distance quartile
within-family versus between-family mean response dissimilarity
number of response-eligible species with complete functional traits
boundaries: A null result applies only to the four frozen life-history/reproductive axes, not all possible traits.
Pairwise entries are non-independent; inference comes from label permutation, not naive pairwise regression P values.
No rainfall causality, phylogenetic mechanism, or evolutionary adaptation claim.
No alternative trait axes or distance metric may replace the frozen panel after readback.
